title: Abstract pointwise cancellation for simultaneous f-divergence
source_anchor: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling (2026-08-09), Theorem 8.3.1 proof, printed p. 219 / PDF p. 230: after the adjoint rewrite, expand L_t(f'(rho) rho) with the definition of Gamma_t, use the generator diffusion chain rule on L_t f(rho), and finally use Gamma_t(f'(rho),rho)=f''(rho) Gamma_t(rho) to obtain the negative dissipation integrand.
target_statement: Formalize only the source-shaped pointwise algebraic cancellation after the adjoint rewrite: for generator L, density ratio rho, numerator density mu and reference density nu with mu=rho*nu at the selected point, consume the corrected Gamma-chain specialization directly, keep the exact #220 product-reconstruction specialization and #221 generator-chain specialization as explicit parent contracts while those branches remain unintegrated, and show that the adjoint integrand collapses to -f''(rho) Gamma(rho,rho) nu. Keep Exercise 2.8 equivalence, time differentiation, adjoint evolution, and integration outside this cell.

shared_floor_audit.notes: This cell deliberately stops before the analytic theorem. The corrected #219 Gamma-chain rule is consumed directly. A previous draft redeclared the product reconstruction locally, but collision review found that this duplicates canonical Frontier Cell #220, so the duplicate declaration was removed. Because #219/#220/#221 are currently parallel unmerged branches, the revised theorem takes the exact #220 and #221 specializations as explicit parent contracts; stabilization can discharge them from canonical declarations once the parents share an integration branch. PR #223 independently discovered the same cancellation but was closed under the deduplication rule because #222 has the stronger parent reuse structure. A proof-script-only failure (`simp made no progress`) was removed without changing the theorem statement; the resulting exact theorem head passed focused and root gates. Convexity of f and f(1)=0 are not used by this local algebraic cancellation and remain reserved for the final source-facing theorem.
